Rashi on Arakhin 18a:11:1.hebrew: אתה היקשתה דמים לערכין - בפ"ק (לעיל ערכין דף ד:), דאמרינן: נדר בערכך נפשות — נדר היינו דמים, בערכך היינו ערכין. היקישן הכתוב להני תרי מילי:
Rashi on Arakhin 18a:11:1.english: You have juxtaposed assessments to valuations - In the first chapter (above, Arakhin 4b), where we say: "A vow, according to your valuation, persons" — "a vow" is [referring to] assessments, [and] "according to your valuation" is [referring to] valuations. Scripture juxtaposed them with regard to these two matters.

Rashi on Arakhin 18a:11:2.hebrew: מרגלית לקלים - דאזלינן במרגלית בתר קלים, דכתיב בערכין: ״ונתן את הערכך ביום ההוא״, ודרשינן לקמן (ערכין דף כד.): ״שלא ישהה מרגלית לקלים״. עני שהעריך עצמו ובא כהן להעריכו, ויש לו מרגלית שוה ל' סלעים — אין אומרים: אם משהין אותה עד שיעלוה לכרך שיש שם עשיר והוא יקננה בנ' סלעים, הילכך נ' סלעים יש לו ויתן ערך שלם — אין אומרים כן, ואין להקדש אלא מקומו ושעתו. וה"נ בדמים: אם אמר ״דמי מרגלית זו עלי״, אין שמין אותה לפי מכר הכרכים, אלא לפי מכר אותה שעה ואותו מקום:
Rashi on Arakhin 18a:11:2.english: A pearl for the light [people] - That with regard to a pearl, we follow the light [i.e., poor people], as it is written regarding valuations: “And he shall give your valuation on that day” (Leviticus 27:23), and we expound below (Arakhin 24a): “That [the treasurer] should not delay a pearl for the light [people].” [In the case of] a poor person who vowed his valuation, and a priest came to evaluate him, and he has a pearl worth thirty sela — we do not say: “If they delay it until they bring it up to a metropolis where there is a wealthy person and he will buy it for fifty sela, therefore he has fifty sela and should give the full valuation” — we do not say so, and the Temple treasury has only its [present] place and its [present] time. And so too regarding [pledges of] value: if one said, “The value of this pearl is upon me,” they do not appraise it according to the sale [prices] of the metropolises, but rather according to the sale [prices] of that time and that place.

Rashi on Arakhin 18a:11:3.hebrew: ולידון בכבודו - שאם העריך דבר שהנשמה תלויה בו — כגון שאמר ״ערך ראשי עלי״ — נותן ערך שלם, דכתיב גבי ערכין: ״בערכך נפשות״, דבתר נפש אזלינן:
Rashi on Arakhin 18a:11:3.english: And to be judged according to its significance - That if one valuated [an organ] upon which life depends — such as if he said, "The valuation of my head is upon me" — he gives a full valuation, as it is written regarding valuations: "[according to] your valuation, souls," for we follow the life.

Rashi on Arakhin 18a:12:1.hebrew: שיתן כשעת נתינה - דבדמים פשיטא לן דיהיב כשעת נתינה ולא כשעת נדר, דהא כעבד בשוק שמין אותו. ואם אמר דמי עלי בתשרי, ובניסן בא לב"ד — מי יודע מה היה שוה בשעת נדר? ושעת נתינה היינו שעה שהוא בא לב"ד:
Rashi on Arakhin 18a:12:1.english: That he should give according to the time of giving - For regarding assessments [damim], it is obvious to us that he gives according to the time of giving and not according to the time of the vow, as they appraise him like a slave in the marketplace. And if he said, "My value is upon me," in Tishrei, and in Nisan he came to court — who knows what he was worth at the time of the vow? And the time of giving means the time that he comes to court.

Rashi on Arakhin 18a:12:2.hebrew: ת"ל כערכך יקום - דמשמע ערכין בשעת ערך — שאם העריך עצמו בן ששים ונעשה יותר על ששים, נותן ערך גדול ולא ערך זקן:
Rashi on Arakhin 18a:12:2.english: The verse states: "According to your valuation it shall stand" - Which implies that valuations [are determined] at the time of valuation — that if he evaluated himself [when he was] sixty years old and became older than sixty, he gives the greater valuation and not the valuation of an elder.

Rashi on Arakhin 18a:13:1.hebrew: יום שלשים כלמטה - ואם אמר: ״ערך פלוני קטן עלי״, ואותו קטן היה באותו יום בן ל' — הוי כלמטה ולא אמר כלום, ואין ערך לפחות מבן חדש, דהכי כתיב: ״ואם מבן חדש וגו'״:
Rashi on Arakhin 18a:13:1.english: The thirtieth day is like [that which is] below it - And if [one] said, “The valuation of so-and-so, a minor, is upon me,” and that minor was thirty [days] old on that day — he is [considered] like [that which is] below it, and [the one who vowed] has said nothing, as there is no valuation for [one who is] less than a month old, for so it is written: “And if [it is] from a month old, etc.”

Rashi on Arakhin 18a:13:2.hebrew: ומעלה - משמע ששלמה שנת ששים, ואז הוא נידון כזקן, אבל בשנת ששים נידון כילד:
Rashi on Arakhin 18a:13:2.english: And upward - [This] implies that the sixtieth year is completed, and then he is judged as an elder; but during the sixtieth year, he is judged as a youth.

Rashi on Arakhin 18a:14:1.hebrew: הן אם עשינו - בתמיה. כלומר: וכי כן הוא? אם עשינו שנת ששים כלמטה להחמיר — דערך גדול יש לו לפחות מבן ששים, נ' סלעים, וליותר על בן ששים אין ערך אלא ט"ו סלעים:
Rashi on Arakhin 18a:14:1.english: Is that so? If we treated - [This is phrased] as a question. That is to say: Is it indeed so? If we treated the sixtieth year like [the category] below it to be stringent — for one who is less than sixty years old has a greater valuation, fifty sela'im, whereas for one who is over sixty years old, the valuation is only fifteen sela'im.

Rashi on Arakhin 18a:15:1.hebrew: להקל - דערך [יותר] על בן כ' יותר גדול הוא מפחות מבן עשרים, וכן בבן חמש, כדכתיב בקראי:
Rashi on Arakhin 18a:15:1.english: To be lenient - For the valuation of [one] over twenty years [old] is greater than [that of one] under twenty years [old], and likewise regarding [one] five years [old], as it is written in the verses.

Rashi on Arakhin 18a:15:2.hebrew: ר"א אומר - לעולם שנת חמש ושנת עשרים ושנת ששים כלמטה, עד שתשלם כל השנה, וחדש ויום א' משנה האחרת:
Rashi on Arakhin 18a:15:2.english: Rabbi Eliezer says - Always, the fifth year, the twentieth year, and the sixtieth year are [considered] like [the period] below, until the entire year is completed, and a month and one day of the next year [have passed].

Rashi on Arakhin 18a:16:1.english: It can be refuted as we refuted [it] - In the mishna.

Rashi on Arakhin 18a:16:2.hebrew: שנה יתירי כתיבי - דמצי למכתב: "ואם מבן ה' שנים ועד בן כ'", ואנא ידענא דעשרים נמי (כ') בשנים משתעי — שנה ל"ל? ובן ששים:
Rashi on Arakhin 18a:16:2.english: [The words] "year" are written superfluous - For it could have written: "And if [it is] from five years old until twenty," and I would know that twenty as well speaks of years; why do I need [the word] "year"? And [likewise with] "and of sixty".

Rashi on Arakhin 18a:17:1.hebrew: לימא מתני' - דמצריך קרא למילף שנת עשרים כלמטה — דלא כרבי? דאי כרבי, האמר: ״עד ועד בכלל״, וכיון דכתיב: ״מבן חמש שנים ועד בן עשרים״ — ממילא ידענא דשנת עשרים בכלל, והיינו כלמטה:
Rashi on Arakhin 18a:17:1.english: Shall we say our mishna - [Which] requires a verse to derive [that] the twentieth year is like [the bracket] below it — [is] not in accordance with Rabbi? For if [it were] in accordance with Rabbi, didn't he say: “[The word] ‘until’ [means] until and including”? And since it is written: “From five years old until twenty [years old],” we would know automatically that the twentieth year is included, and that is “like [the bracket] below it.”

Rashi on Arakhin 18a:18:1.hebrew: יכול - מיום הראשון ואילך יהא מוזהר על חמץ, ולא ראשון בכלל:
Rashi on Arakhin 18a:18:1.english: One might [think] - [That] from the first day and onward one would be prohibited from [eating] leaven, and the first [day] is not included.

Rashi on Arakhin 18a:1:1.english: And afterward his daughter died - Before he came to court to testify.

Rashi on Arakhin 18a:3:2.hebrew: יכול יהו חייבין - העדים קרבן שבועת העדות, אם לא העידוהו:
Rashi on Arakhin 18a:3:2.english: [One might think] they would be liable - The witnesses [would be liable to bring] an offering of an oath of testimony, if they did not testify for him.

Rashi on Arakhin 18a:3:3.english: And behold, he did not single out his witnesses - For he adjured all of them.

Rashi on Arakhin 18a:4:1.hebrew: יכול אפי' אמר כל מי - שיודע עדות אני משביע, לא יהו חייבין:
Rashi on Arakhin 18a:4:1.english: [One might think that] even if he said, “Whoever...” - [“...whoever] knows testimony, I adjure [him],” they would not be liable.

Rashi on Arakhin 18a:4:2.english: The verse states: "And he is a witness," and behold, he singled out his witnesses - For he adjured only his witnesses.

Rashi on Arakhin 18a:5:1.english: He is wealthy - And why does the Temple treasury have no share in them?

Rashi on Arakhin 18a:5:2.hebrew: מניח - שעדיין לא מת אביו, אבל עתיד הוא להניח לו:
Rashi on Arakhin 18a:5:2.english: [He is] leaving - For his father has not yet died, but he is destined to leave [it] to him.

Rashi on Arakhin 18a:6:1.english: [It is] obvious - For he does not have [it].

Rashi on Arakhin 18a:6:2.english: When his father was moribund - At the time that the priest evaluates him.

Rashi on Arakhin 18a:7:1.hebrew: כשהיתה - ספינתו מוחכרת ביד אחרים, ואין לו בתוכה כלום אלא שכרה. והיינו ריבוא דקתני במתני':
Rashi on Arakhin 18a:7:1.english: When it was - His ship was leased to others, and he has nothing inside it except for its rent. And that is the 'ten thousand' that is taught in the mishna.

Rashi on Arakhin 18a:8:1.hebrew: הא מני ר"א היא - דאמר לקמן בפ' שום היתומים (ערכין דף כג:) גבי ערכין: אם היה חמר, נותן לו הכהן חמורו, ואינו נוטלה להקדש:
Rashi on Arakhin 18a:8:1.english: Whose [opinion] is this? It is Rabbi Eliezer - For he says below in the chapter [entitled] Shum HaYetomim (Arakhin 23b) with regard to valuations: If he was a donkey driver, the priest gives him his donkey, and does not take it for the Temple treasury.

Rashi on Arakhin 18a:8:2.english: His pair - A pair of oxen, for that is his livelihood.

Rashi on Arakhin 18a:9:1.hebrew: ילד - מבן כ' ועד בן ששים, דהוי ערכו נ' שקלים:
Rashi on Arakhin 18a:9:1.english: A youth - [One] from twenty to sixty years old, whose valuation is fifty shekels.

Rashi on Arakhin 18a:9:2.english: The valuations [are determined] by the one valuated - And we do not follow the valuator regarding the fixed rate of the valuation.

Tosafot on Arakhin 18a:12:1.hebrew: שיתן כשעת נתינה - פי' רש"י, דבדמים פשיטא ליה דיהיב כשעת נתינה ולא כשעת הנדר, דהא כעבד בשוק שמין אותו; ואם אמר "דמי עלי" בתשרי ובניסן בא לב"ד — מי יודע מה היה שוה בשעת הנדר? ושעת נתינה היינו [שעה] שהוא בא לב"ד — לשון רש"י. ותימה: מאי סברא הוא זה? דלמה יש לנו לומר שהיה שוה יותר מעכשיו? ואם אנו רואים שהוא חלש עכשיו ואז היה גבור, אז ידענו בודאי שהיה שוה יותר — ונפסיד ההקדש מאחר שאנו רואים שהיה שוה יותר סלע לכל הפחות?! לכך אור"י, דאין זו סברא, אלא שום ראיה מקרא יש בו. ועוד, דתנן לקמן פרק האומר משקלי (ערכין דף כ. ושם): "מת הנידר, לא יתנו היורשים, לפי שאין דמים למתים". ואם היה הטעם מסברא דאזלינן בתר נתינה, התם לא שייך למימר הך סברא, שהרי ידענו שהיה שוה בחייו סלע לכל הפחות! וא"כ, מפני מה אנו פוטרים היורשים מכל וכל? אלא ודאי, שום קרא יש בו:
Tosafot on Arakhin 18a:12:1.english: "That he should give according to the time of giving" - Rashi explained that with regard to assessments, it is obvious to [the Gemara] that he gives according to the time of giving and not according to the time of the vow, for he is appraised like a slave in the marketplace; and if he said, "My assessment is upon me" in Tishrei, and in Nisan came to court, who knows what he was worth at the time of the vow? And "the time of giving" is [the time] that he comes to court — [this is] Rashi's phrasing. And it is astonishing: What reasoning is this? For why should we say that he was worth more [then] than now? And if we see that he is weak now, whereas back then he was strong, then we know with certainty that he was worth more — and shall we cause a loss to consecrated property, given that we see that he was worth at least a sela more?! Therefore the Ri says that this is not [a matter of] reasoning, but rather there is some proof from Scripture for it. And furthermore, we learned in a mishna later, in the chapter [entitled] "HaOmer Mishkali" (Arakhin 20a and there): "If the one whose assessment was vowed died, the heirs shall not give, because the dead have no monetary value." And if the reason that we follow [the value at the time of] giving were based on reasoning, there it is not applicable to say this reasoning, for we knew that he was worth at least a sela during his lifetime! And if so, why do we exempt the heirs entirely? Rather, there is certainly some verse for it.

Tosafot on Arakhin 18a:18:1.hebrew: יכול ראשון ולא ראשון בכלל שביעי ולא שביעי בכלל - וא"ת: היאך אפשר לומר כן, והכתיב (שמות י״ג:ו׳): "שבעת ימים תאכל מצות"? וי"ל: דלחיוב כרת קאמר, דכרת בהאי קרא כתיב, דכתיב: "כי כל אוכל מחמצת ונכרתה מיום הראשון עד יום השביעי". מש"ה מייתי ת"ל: "עד יום האחד ועשרים בערב", והאי קרא — כרת נמי כתיב ביה:
Tosafot on Arakhin 18a:18:1.english: "One might [think]: The first, but the first is not included; the seventh, but the seventh is not included" - And if you say: How is it possible to say so, when it is written (Exodus 13:6): "Seven days you shall eat matzot"? And one can say: It is speaking of liability to karet [spiritual excision], for karet is written in this verse, as it is written: "For whoever eats leavened bread, that soul shall be cut off [...] from the first day until the seventh day" [Exodus 12:15]. That is why [the baraita] cites: The verse states: "until the twenty-first day in the evening" [Exodus 12:18] — and this verse [passage] also has karet written in it.

Tosafot on Arakhin 18a:2:1.hebrew: ואלא והוא ל"ל לרבי כדאית ליה ולרבנן כדאית להו - וקשיא: לרבי, מאי דרשי רבנן (הכא הוא) "ואם מך הוא מערכך"? ושמא יש דרשא בשום מקום מהאי "הוא" דהכא, ודרשי' ליה:
Tosafot on Arakhin 18a:2:1.english: "But rather, why do I need 'and he'? According to Rabbi, in accordance with his [view], and according to the Rabbis, in accordance with their [view]" - And it is difficult: according to Rabbi, what do the Rabbis derive (here, [from] 'he' [in]) "And if he is too poor for your valuation"? And perhaps there is an exposition somewhere from this 'he' here, and they expound it.

Tosafot on Arakhin 18a:6:1.hebrew: לא צריכא שהיה אביו גוסס כו' - פירש בקונט': אבל בערכין, בדעת הכהן תליא רחמנא; ואי חזי דאביו גוסס, אינו מעריכו עד שימות אביו. ולא נהירא; דלקמן אמרינן: "אין בהקדש אלא מקומו ושעתו", ובסמוך נמי מייתי לה: "אתה הקשת דמים לערכין ומרגלית לקלים". פירוש: עני שהעריך עצמו, ויש לו מרגלית שאינה שוה עכשיו כי אם כ' סלעים — אין אומרים נמתין עד שיבא יום השוק ותעלה לנ' סלעים, אלא שמין אותה כמו שהיא עכשיו, ולא יתן כ"א כ' סלעים. וא"כ, למה אנו צריכין להמתין עד שימות אביו? לכן נראה לר"י, דלא קאי "אבל בקרבנות אינו כן" אמת אביו, אלא אהא דלעיל קאי, וסוף מילתא דר' יהודה היא; והא דמפרש אח"כ: "אפי' מת אביו והניח לו כו'" — מילתא באפי נפשה היא, וקרבנות וערכין שוין בו:
Tosafot on Arakhin 18a:6:1.english: "No, it is necessary [in a case] where his father was moribund, etc." - The Kuntres explained: However, with regard to valuations, the Merciful One made [the assessment] depend on the discretion of the priest; and if he sees that his father is moribund, he does not valuate him until his father dies. But this does not seem correct, for later [24a] we say: "For consecrated property, there is only its place and its time," and nearby [18a] it also cites this: "You compared damim [pledges of value] to arakhin [valuations], and a pearl to draperies [or tapestries]." Explanation: A poor person who valuated himself and possesses a pearl that is currently worth only twenty sela'im, we do not say: "Let us wait until the market day arrives and it will rise to fifty sela'im"; rather, they appraise it as it is right now, and he gives only twenty sela'im. And if so, why must we wait until his father dies? Therefore, it appears to the Ri that "But with regard to offerings that is not so" does not refer to [the clause] "his father died"; rather, it refers to that which is [stated] above, and it is the conclusion of Rabbi Yehuda's statement. And that which [the Mishnah] explains afterward, "Even [if] his father died and left him, etc.," is an independent matter, and offerings and valuations are equal regarding it.
